records.title: Humanities First: Foundations
records.text: HUM 101 Humanities First: Foundations (3) A&H Topics change yearly, but course is anchored in four themes at the foundation of the humanistic endeavor: language, objects, space, and time. Focuses on what Humanists do, how they do it, various techniques and use of evidence, primary goals, and public-facing results. Offered: A.

records.title: Humanities First: Campus Connections
records.header: HUM 102 Humanities First: Campus Connections (2) SSc
records.text: HUM 102 Humanities First: Campus Connections (2) SSc A "laboratory seminar" that combines a core text with visits to campus partners to explore the work of humanists in the world. Students work on e-portfolio and the practice of public humanities communications. Recommended: HUM 101. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: W.

records.text: HUM 103 Humanities First: Community Connections (2) SSc A "laboratory seminar" that combines a core text with visits to community partners in Seattle and beyond to explore the work of humanists in the world. records.title: Introduction to Studies in the Humanities
records.header: HUM 201 Introduction to Studies in the Humanities (5) A&H
records.text: HUM 201 Introduction to Studies in the Humanities (5) A&H Introduction to fundamental concepts and approaches to the study of the humanities. Topics covered drawn from literature, language, history, culture, civilization, and other central areas of the humanities.

records.title: Religion, Violence, and Peace: Patterns Across Time and Tradition
records.header: HUM 205 Religion, Violence, and Peace: Patterns Across Time and Tradition (5) SSc
records.text: HUM 205 Religion, Violence, and Peace: Patterns Across Time and Tradition (5) SSc Investigates the complex relationship between violence and peace in a variety of religious traditions. Examines case studies from the ancient Near East, medieval East Asia, and the contemporary West from the standpoint of lived experiences and contemporary theories derived from several academic disciplines. Offered: jointly with MELC 285/RELIG 205; W.

records.title: Humanities Next: Outreach, Communication, and Mentorship
records.header: HUM 208 Humanities Next: Outreach, Communication, and Mentorship (1, max. 6)
records.text: HUM 208 Humanities Next: Outreach, Communication, and Mentorship (1, max. 6) Introduces students to the basic techniques of public humanities outreach and communication, as well as to the leadership skills and strategies involved in on-campus peer mentorship with incoming first-year students enrolled in Humanities First. Prerequisite: HUM 101; HUM 102; and HUM 103. Credit/no-credit only. Offered: AWSp.
